relations.why: Solo devs and cash-poor founders are two segments of one set-valued predicate. Both stand.
Same segment said twice, second phrasing is the sharper one. Value should become the union.
A positive and a negative that define the same boundary from two sides. Not a conflict — the pair IS the definition.
Different predicates entirely — one is the audience, the other is how the audience may be defined.
USA alone, then USA inside the core three. The later claim contains the earlier.
THE headline case: hedged 'not sure we can enter China', then 'China we can'. Six turns apart, in different sessions of the same conversation.
Same turn asserts China is a core market AND doubts entry. A human must say which layer this lives on — ambition vs feasibility.
'post-CIS is a secondary market' vs 'everything except CIS'. Different predicates on paper, same real-world claim — the hard one.
Ukraine is a carve-out from the CIS exclusion, not a contradiction of it. Needs the human to say so.
'proprietary + open source' refined into 'proprietary + subscription, free at first'. Same decision, sharpened.
Two free-tier populations, set-valued predicate, no tension.
Not a contradiction of values — a stated risk against a stated decision. The base should surface it, and a human decides.
Different subjects: base Mesh vs enterprise Mesh. This is the Airbnb buyers/sellers shape, in real data.

accepted_gaps.why: Note 42 proposes resellers as an audience; note 44 rejects the direction without naming it, saying only that the product must not become ETN. Recorded self-contained, the two claims share no address and no mechanical pass will ever pair them. The operator accepts this: a human or a verifier sweeping the base later marks the link.

'not sure we can enter China' (go-to-market) vs 'China we can' (regulatory coverage). Self-contained extraction puts them under different subjects, so the reversal does not surface mechanically. Same accepted gap.
